What makes sharks so amazing?

The shark, the sea's magnificent hunter, is a fascinating fish that swims fast. Unlike in the movies, most sharks don't harm people at all.

content.alt: Shark - Nature and science facts about sharks
content.text:
Nature and science facts about sharks

The bones that support a shark's body aren't hard bone but soft cartilage, so it swims smoothly and fast. When a tooth falls out, a new one keeps coming up from behind, so its teeth are replaced many times throughout its life. It has an excellent sense of smell that helps it find prey far away, and its skin is rough with tiny scales. The biggest, the whale shark, is a gentle shark that strains tiny plankton to eat, and sharks are important animals that keep the ocean ecosystem in balance.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What happens when a shark's tooth falls out?
A. A new tooth keeps coming up from behind, so its teeth are replaced many times throughout its life. It always has new teeth.

Q. Are all sharks scary?
A. No. Most don't harm people, and the biggest, the whale shark, is a gentle shark that strains plankton to eat.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Compare "movie vs. real sharks" and compare tooth replacement to your child losing baby teeth.
